# AI/LLM Integration

Covers dimension 11 (AI/LLM integration). Sources referenced in
[citations.md](../citations.md).

## Overview

Inngest positions AI orchestration as a first-class use case, providing three
layers of AI integration: step-level AI primitives, the AgentKit framework,
and MCP integration [11][12][13].

## Step-Level AI Primitives

### step.ai.infer()

Offloads inference requests to Inngest's infrastructure, pausing function
execution until completion [11]. This eliminates serverless function compute
costs during LLM response waiting periods.

Supported providers for step.ai.infer() [11]:
- OpenAI (including OpenAI-compatible APIs like Perplexity)
- Anthropic
- Gemini
- Grok
- Azure OpenAI

```typescript
const response = await step.ai.infer("call-openai", {
  model: step.ai.models.openai({ model: "gpt-4o" }),
  body: {
    messages: [{
      role: "assistant",
      content: "Write instructions for improving short term memory",
    }],
  },
});
```

### step.ai.wrap()

Wraps existing AI SDKs as retriable steps with observability, preserving
existing code patterns [11]:

Supported wrap SDKs [11]:
- Vercel AI SDK
- Anthropic SDK
- OpenAI SDK

### Observability

Both methods automatically track [11]:
- Prompts and responses
- Token usage metrics
- Multi-step agentic workflow integration

### Limitations

- Streaming responses "coming soon" [11]
- step.ai.wrap() arguments must be JSON-serializable [11]
- Complex function overloads may require TypeScript type casting [11]

## AgentKit

TypeScript framework for building AI agent systems [12]:

### Components

| Component | Role | Source |
|-----------|------|--------|
| Agents | Individual AI entities with system prompts and tool access | [12] |
| Networks | Collections of agents coordinated toward shared objectives | [12] |
| Routers | Decision-making for request delegation within networks | [12] |
| State | Persistent memory layer tracking network activity | [12] |
| Tools | Extensible API layer with MCP integration | [12] |

### Supported LLM Providers [12]

- OpenAI (gpt-4o, gpt-3.5-turbo)
- Anthropic (claude-3-5-haiku-latest)
- Google Gemini
- All OpenAI API-compatible models

### Maturity

AgentKit was released in "early access" around January 2026 [37]. No version
number or stability classification found in documentation [12]. Integration
partnerships with E2B, Browserbase, Smithery, Daytona suggest some production
usage [12].

## MCP Integration

Three MCP touchpoints identified [13]:

### 1. Dev Server MCP

The Inngest Dev Server exposes an MCP endpoint at `http://127.0.0.1:8288/mcp`
with 8 tools [13]:

| Category | Tools |
|----------|-------|
| Event management | send_event, list_functions, invoke_function |
| Execution monitoring | get_run_status, poll_run_status |
| Documentation | grep_docs, read_doc, list_docs |

Configuration for Claude Code [13]:
```bash
claude mcp add --transport http inngest-dev http://127.0.0.1:8288/mcp
```

- No API keys required [13]
- Local-only operation [13]
- Default 30-second polling/invocation timeout [13]
- Requires dev server actively running [13]

### 2. AgentKit MCP Tools

AgentKit can consume any MCP server as tools for agents [12]. References
Smithery registry with 2000+ available MCP servers.

### 3. Documentation MCP Server

Inngest documentation available as MCP resource for AI coding agents [13].

## Assessment for Personal Assistant Use Case

The user's PA is the LLM layer; the engine runs deterministic pipelines.
AI/LLM integration is nice-to-have, not required.

| Feature | Relevance | Notes |
|---------|-----------|-------|
| step.ai.infer() | Low | PA already handles LLM calls directly |
| step.ai.wrap() | Low | Same — PA is the AI layer |
| AgentKit | Low | PA doesn't need agent orchestration in the workflow engine |
| Dev Server MCP | Medium | Useful for PA to trigger/monitor workflows |
| AgentKit MCP | Low | PA already has its own tool access |

The Dev Server MCP is the most relevant feature — it would let the PA
(Claude Code) list functions, trigger them, and monitor runs via MCP tools
without writing custom API integration.

## Gaps and Limitations

- **AgentKit is TypeScript-only** — no Python or Go agent framework
- **AgentKit is early access** — API stability not guaranteed
- **step.ai.infer() architecture unclear** — described as "offloading" inference
  to Inngest infrastructure, but unclear if this is a proxy, managed inference,
  or async execution wrapper
- **MCP is dev-server only** — no production MCP endpoint mentioned
- **No native LLM nodes** like n8n's 70+ LangChain-integrated nodes — Inngest
  provides primitives, not pre-built integrations
